title: Save-path contract net: id coverage AND no-op round-trip (new registered suite)
goal: A new root suite _forgeids_smoke.mjs registered in _checkall.mjs with expect 0, in TWO halves. HALF A (id coverage): every string-literal id read by captureEditorIntoCard — derived at run time by lifting the function source between 150654 and 152135 and regexing every v('…'), num('…') and getElementById('…') — exists in the HTML renderCardEditor() produces; plus the class-based readback hooks invisible to the id convention (.learn-row/.learn-move 152136, #elem-mods-rows .elem-mod-row + .em-* 152145, .sub-card[data-sub-idx] 150214, #trigger-rows .trg-row, #fusion-req-rows .fusion-req-row, #archon-req-rows .archon-req-row, .ed-treatas-zone, .ed-value-axis, #ed-factions [data-faction], #ed-traitpool [data-traitpool]); plus the nine ability drawers exist by name after bindCardEditor(). HALF B — THE ONE THE OLD PLAN LACKED (no-op round-trip): load every card in Forge.customCards and the built-in catalogue into renderCardEditor/bindCardEditor, run captureEditorIntoCard with ZERO user input, and assert the serialised card is identical to the input. This is the only test that can catch the 77 literal-fallback num() sites (150667; e.g. num('ed-ig-chance',1,100,100), num('ed-onplay-amount',0,200,6)) silently rewriting a live card definition to a constant when a layout piece removes a field from the DOM — and saveCardFromInputs cloud-pushes immediately at 152231-152245, so the damaged definition reaches every owner.
bar: On unmodified HEAD: ALL PASS, exit 0, and the suite PRINTS the derived id count and asserts it is >= 200 (a lifter that silently returns an empty list must not pass — the old '25 PASS lines' floor was arbitrary and unvalidated). Half B prints ALL-IDENTICAL over >= 30 real cards including at least one of each type (unit, spell, trap, summon, weather, hero). TWO DISCRIMINATING TESTS, both in-memory (NOT sed -i on a 15 MB mixed-CRLF file): (1) mutate the captured renderCardEditor() output string to rename one id and re-run half A — it must print a FAIL line NAMING that id; (2) monkey-patch renderCardEditor to omit one numeric field's markup and re-run half B — it must print a FAIL line naming that field and showing old→new value. A suite that passes both before and after either mutation has not earned its place.

title: A Forge driver harness that actually reaches the editor (and can A/B safely)
goal: Every screenshot bar in the previous plan was unreachable and would have failed SILENTLY. renderForge() is admin-gated at 144667-144673: a non-admin gets showToast + App.screen='title' + setTimeout(render,0) + return — no error, no throw. A driver built on .gauntlet/_shot-screen.mjs (`App.screen=s; render()`) screenshots the TITLE SCREEN and reports success. Build .gauntlet/_forge-harness.mjs exporting: openCardEditor(page, cardId) which sets Profile.cloud={signedIn:true,email:<an ADMIN_EMAILS entry>}, renders, and HARD-ASSERTS App.screen==='forge' && document.querySelector('.card-editor') before returning; seedNonAdmin(profile) for ownership-gated UI (deckKeyOwnedCount returns Infinity for admins at 59966, so pieces 20 and 21 cannot be judged from the owner's own client); forceOpen(selector) which sets details.open=true on every .fx-sec/.fx-sub being measured and appends the host to document.body (_fxOpen at 133951 returns '' unless App._fxOpen was populated, so every section renders CLOSED, and App._fxOpen accumulates across cards and is never cleared — offsetParent is null for everything inside a closed <details> and for every element in a detached host, so an unforced A/B compares two different open-sets, or 0 against 0); and abRun(driver) which creates `git worktree add ../head-ab HEAD` and runs the same driver with cwd set there. NO PIECE MAY USE `git stash` FOR A/B — it is whole-tree on a repo whose own .gauntlet/precommit-scan.mjs exists because other agents write here, and deploy.mjs:16-49 minifies public/index.html in place, so a stash racing a deploy is unrecoverable.
bar: Mechanically self-proving. (1) Called with a non-admin profile, openCardEditor THROWS with a message naming the admin gate — it must not return a page. (2) Called with the admin profile it returns and `document.querySelectorAll('.editor-field').length` is > 100. (3) forceOpen makes `[...document.querySelectorAll('#fx-onplay .editor-field')].filter(e=>e.offsetParent!==null).length` > 0 where the same query without forceOpen returns 0 — print both numbers. (4) abRun on an UNCHANGED tree returns byte-identical metrics from both sides (a harness whose A/B reports a difference on a no-op diff is measuring noise). (5) `git worktree list` shows the HEAD worktree created and removed cleanly; `git status` on the main tree is unchanged by the A/B run.

title: Unlock the editor width and make the field grid responsive — with a legibility floor
goal: `.card-editor { max-width: 900px; margin: 0 auto }` at 33891-33898 still applies to `.card-editor.fx-two` — 19553-19556 sets display/grid-template-columns only and does NOT override max-width. So on any monitor the editor is 900px: a fixed 380px sticky asset rail plus ~500px of properties holding 343 fields in a 2-column grid, ~230px per column. That declaration IS the owner's 'doesn't fit the screen'. Scope an override to .fx-two and let the field grid gain COLUMNS, not just width: `.editor-grid` is `repeat(2, 1fr)` at 33912 and is SHARED by renderMoveEditor, the event editor and the elem-mod rows, so the column-count change must be scoped `.fx-two .editor-grid` or it leaks. Widening alone cannot hit a scrollHeight target — wider columns, same row count. State a rule for the many `.editor-field.full` blocks (grid-column 1/-1), which stretch absurdly at 4 columns. The 1080px media query at 19585 collapses to one column with a static unbounded .fx-assets rail; that path needs its own answer, not just 'no horizontal scrollbar'.
bar: Measured through the harness with forced-open state, plus a legibility floor that makes the density number unpurchasable by shrinking type. DENSITY: at 1600x1000 with a FIXED, EXPLICIT open-set (identity + kind + effects + on-play forced open, everything else forced closed, identical on both sides of the A/B), computed width of `.card-editor.fx-two` > 1300px where HEAD is exactly 900px, and `.fx-props` scrollHeight for the SAME card with the SAME open-set drops >= 30%. LEGIBILITY FLOOR (all four widths): no `.fx-two .editor-grid` computed column narrower than 260px; no label element whose scrollWidth exceeds its clientWidth (nothing truncated) and none wrapping past 2 lines; no input or select with computed height < 28px; computed font-size on labels and controls is >= HEAD's. CONTROLS: the move editor's `.card-editor` (152445) and the event editor's (153673) are still 900px; no horizontal page scrollbar at 1600/1280/1080/720; at 1080 and 720 the .fx-assets rail is not full-height above the properties column (assert .fx-props top < viewport height); the trait-pool modal still escapes to <body> — assert `modal.offsetParent === document.body` and its getBoundingClientRect() is inside the viewport (adding transform/filter/contain to any .card-editor ancestor re-traps it, see 150447-150452). NOTE the `.fx-actions` save bar is `position:sticky;bottom:0` (19574) so 'reachable without scrolling' is true on HEAD and after any change — it is a CONTROL, not a bar.

Every author sees Board Wipe scope (147355), Sacrifice effect (147369), Call Seal (147443), Buff target (147431), Paint Surface (147139), Negate-Field scope (147194), Vanish+Return (147206), Search-Deck type (147083), Summon-From-Zone (147117), Cheapen Duration (147004) and the rest for EVERY effect — in the primary on-play block, in the five SIBLING blocks (148110, 148166, 148305, 148318, 148511) AND in the six onPlayExtra slots. All of them are in scope; gating only the primary block passes a naive count bar while leaving the wall intact. Gate live on the select's change event with no full re-render. THREE HARD CONSTRAINTS. (1) Hidden fields MUST stay in the DOM — not conditionally rendered. Remove a numeric field and num() returns its LITERAL fallback (150667), silently rewriting the card and cloud-pushing it (152231). This is the single most dangerous line in the whole job. (2) They must still count as .editor-field descendants or the empty-section sweep at 150611-150614 sets display:none on the whole section. (3) The sweep and the nav-chip hider at 150615-150618 both run ONCE inside bindCardEditor. Gating live without re-running them leaves a visible drawer full of nothing when an effect empties a sub-section — the exact bug 150607's comment was written to fix — and leaves a live chip pointing at a hidden section. The change handler must re-run both passes.
bar: THE PERCENTAGE BAR IS REPLACED BY A PER-EFFECT WHITELIST, because a single ratio on one favourable effect (drawCards, the effect with the fewest fields) is gameable. FOR EVERY ONE of the ~118 ONPLAY_TYPES ids: after setting the select by assigning .value AND dispatching input+change (assigning .value alone fires nothing and tests a dead form), the set of VISIBLE field ids inside the on-play block equals the set that effect's save path actually reads — derivable from the gating at 151392-151553. Same assertion for the five sibling blocks and the six extra slots, not just #fx-onplay. SWEEP COHERENCE, for every effect id: no .fx-sec/.fx-sub is visible with zero visible .editor-field, and no visible nav chip points at a hidden section. NO LIVE-DATA DAMAGE — the assertion that settles the piece: `node _forgeids_smoke.mjs` half B stays ALL-IDENTICAL over all >= 30 real cards. A builder who implements gating by conditional template rendering (the natural way) will pass every visible-field count and FAIL this. ROUND-TRIP: type a value under effect A, switch to B, switch back to A, run captureEditorIntoCard, assert the value is present in the captured object — done in-memory in the driver, NOT by saving to live Forge data. NOTHING GOES BLANK: the nine ability drawers still appear by name (the runtime split at 150550 buckets TOP-LEVEL children of #fx-ingrave .editor-grid by probing [id^="ed-ig-"] — one extra wrapper div collapses all nine into a single 'In-Grave' drawer, the exact bug that code fixes).

title: Hard stop: show the owner the gating model and get four decisions in writing
goal: The owner said 'do a loop'. Pieces 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 19, 20 and 21 all build on decisions I cannot make alone. Deliver real screenshots of the widened + gated editor (pieces 3-4) and get four answers recorded in the code comments the way this file does. (i) THE MOVE MODEL: 'either they are an ability, physical, or magic' is ONE mutually-exclusive control, but the data is two orthogonal axes — mv-kind (152455) offers attack/ability/summon while teleport, phaseStep and grapplingHook carry kind:'movement' with no option, and mv-type (152478) offers physical/magic only. A literal 3-way control cannot express 'ability + magic' and destroys kind:'summon' and kind:'movement'. Is 'ability' a kind or a damage channel? (ii) AI DECK SIZE at 40-80: a go/no-go, not a preference. Deck-out loses the match (_drawFailed at 101347, end at 120388); AI pinned at 40 against a player at 80 means the paying player cannot lose the fatigue race, and copies come from paid packs. Match the AI, or cap the max below 80. (iii) Does the Realm Deck's 21 count toward the 40-80 total? Piece 20 assumes OUTSIDE (a separate roster, as today). (iv) REALM OWNERSHIP: ownership is ALREADY fully enforced (245471-245476 computes deckKeyOwnedCount, renders '🔒 Not owned', greys the row, disables +; handler re-checks at 246156-246158). So does 'just like how they add to their main deck' mean UX PARITY (the Realm roster is added from a 340px scrolling list at 245503 instead of the main deck's card grid + search + right-click detail) or a SHARED owned-copy budget across main+side+realm? The shared-budget reading retroactively invalidates decks players built and paid for; I will not choose it unilaterally.
bar: Not a code bar — a decision bar, and it is checkable. Four screenshots exist and show the REAL editor (harness-asserted App.screen==='forge' and a .card-editor in the DOM, not the title screen). Four answers are recorded verbatim in the plan and, where they change behaviour, as a comment at the site they govern. Pieces 6, 7, 10-12, 16, 17, 19, 20 and 21 do not start until all four are recorded. A checkpoint that produces screenshots but no written decisions has not happened.

title: Stop the move editor silently rewriting abilities into physical attacks

title: Audit and repair the moves the editor has ALREADY corrupted
goal: Piece 11 stops 152869 stamping type:'physical' onto abilities in FUTURE. It does nothing about the Forge.customMoves overrides that already carry it, and lookupMove (80577) prefers customMoves over the built-in for the entire game — so every ability the owner has opened and saved since this shipped is already a physical-channel move in live play, for every player. Fix-forward-only leaves the damage in the data. Produce an audit that diffs every Forge.customMoves override against its built-in on kind, type and element, classify each difference as INTENDED (the author changed something else too) or ARTEFACT (the override is identical to the built-in except for a field the save path writes unconditionally — type appearing where the built-in has none, kind:'attack' where the built-in has 'movement', element:'fire' where the built-in has 'none'), and repair the artefacts. Must run AFTER piece 11 — repairing before the corrupter is fixed just re-corrupts on the next save.
bar: The audit is a printed table, not a claim: every override key with {field, builtinValue, overrideValue, classification}, and the counts per classification. Repair touches ONLY rows classified ARTEFACT, and the definition of ARTEFACT is mechanical (the override equals the built-in on every field EXCEPT ones the 152869 literal writes unconditionally) so a critic can recompute the classification independently and get the same set. After repair, re-running the audit yields zero ARTEFACT rows and the same INTENDED rows as before (an audit that also 'repairs' an intended edit has destroyed the owner's work). Before/after, `lookupMove` returns the built-in's kind/type/element for every repaired id. A dry-run mode prints the table WITHOUT writing, and the dry run is what the critic reviews before the write happens. `node _duel_smoke.mjs`, `node _skilltree_smoke.mjs` and `node _moveeditor_smoke.mjs` all pass after.

No such prompt exists: discardCards (110990) is random and hits the opponent; discardSelf (111141) is random from your own hand. The picker exists and is already used this exact way — _openDeckSearchModal('any', ids, name, 'grave', N, 'hand', filter, 0) at 111203 — guarded `owner === 'player' && !eff._autoPick` with a deterministic AI path at 111208. The reducer is SYNCHRONOUS and returns state, so it must open a QUEUED prompt and return, never await.
bar: CORRECTED MULTIPLAYER RULE — the previous bar was inverted and would have SHIPPED A BUG. It said every hand removal must call _mpNotePrivateRemoval (205197). That primitive is explicitly and only for removals from the OPPONENT's zone: the contract at 205180-205192 says the op list is 'deliberately REMOVALS ONLY' from the victim's zone performed inside the actor's engine, and the call-site comment at 111013-111015 says 'targetSide is ALWAYS the foe here'. _mpApplyPrivateRemovals applies each op to the RECEIVER's own block, matching instanceId then falling back to op.cardId at 205228 which removes a single copy BY DEFINITION ID. Effect (a) discards from the ACTOR's OWN hand, so relaying it makes the opponent's client delete a copy of that card from THEIR hand — guaranteed on any shared definition id. THE BAR IS THEREFORE THE OPPOSITE: after a self-discard, assert `state._mpPrivateRemovals` is empty/unchanged, exactly as discardSelf (111141) already does. THE HAND-CAP POLICY IS DECIDED, not left open: drawCards at 101347 shifts a card off the deck and pushes it NOWHERE once the hand hits 8 (HAND_LIMIT 7 at 160336), and the branch clamp is 1..5 at 111043 while the editor allows 0..200. Pick ONE of draw-fewer / discard-first-then-draw / overdraw-then-force-discard, write the reason in the code comment the way this file does, and assert the chosen one: with the hand at 8, the driver reports zero cards vanishing to nowhere (deck+hand+grave total is conserved). EVIDENCE, NOT BOOLEANS: the driver dumps the actual App.ui.deckSearch object and the queue length (not `secondPromptShown`), the before/after arrays of hand instanceIds (not `handAfter` as a number), and a counting wrapper's call log for _mpNotePrivateRemoval (not `mpRelayCalled`). NEGATIVE CONTROLS THAT MUST FLIP: bypass _deckSearchEnqueue (162906) and write App.ui.deckSearch directly — the second prompt must vanish and the driver must REPORT that (the documented bug at 162893-162905); force _autoPick off on the AI side and the modal must appear. A driver whose numbers cannot be made to fail has proved nothing. `node .gauntlet/drive-hand-wipe.mjs` must still pass — it enumerates every ONPLAY_TYPES id through the real placeUnit asserting no effect empties hand and graveyard together, and this effect legitimately shrinks the hand.

title: An authorable 'send cards from the Void back to your deck' effect — the event (c) needs
goal: NEW PIECE, and effect (c) is dead without it. I grepped every void-to-deck movement in the file: there is EXACTLY ONE — `if (wants('void') && Array.isArray(st.void) && st.void.length) { moved += st.void.length; deck = deck.concat(st.void); }` at 111991, inside the shuffleToDeck branch, whose zone default was changed to 'grave' at 111917 after the v121f4 hand-wipe (34-line incident comment at 111881-111915). recycleVoid sends void→graveyard, not deck. So a void→deck trigger (piece 17) can only ever fire when some OTHER card happens to be authored with shuffleZones = void/graveVoid/all — the owner's clause would ship as a trigger with no reliable in-game event. Add a first-class, gated, author-facing effect that returns N cards (or all) from a chosen side's Void to that side's deck, built on the existing shuffleToDeck plumbing rather than a second destructive branch, with an explicit zone knob and NO destructive default.
bar: The knob is never absent-and-destructive — the lesson of 111881-111915, where a missing knob defaulted to 'sweep everything' and wiped a live hand. Assert: with the knob absent (which is how it arrives from an onPlayExtra slot, whose knob list at 151577-151602 is much shorter than the primary's), the effect moves ZERO cards and logs a no-op, never a sweep. With the knob set to N, exactly N cards move void→deck for the CHOSEN side and nothing else moves — hand, graveyard and units are byte-identical before and after (dumped as arrays). Cross-side: targeting your own void does not touch the opponent's, and vice versa; the log line distinguishes them (the `sd === owner ? 'your' : "the enemy's"` shape at 112001). Authorable end-to-end IN THE REAL EDITOR: the driver opens the card editor through the harness, selects the new effect, sets the knob, runs captureEditorIntoCard, and asserts the knob is written to card.onPlay GATED on the effect id — then feeds that captured card into the battle driver and it resolves. `node .gauntlet/drive-shufflezones.mjs`, `node .gauntlet/verify-shuffle-default.mjs` and `node .gauntlet/drive-hand-wipe.mjs` all pass.

'your' : "the enemy's"` at 112001). SAFE WITH THE KNOB ABSENT: authored in an onPlayExtra slot (short knob list at 151577-151602) the trigger must no-op, not sweep. title: Adding Realm cards feels like adding main-deck cards (and the budget question, answered)

So 'just like how they add to their main deck' is most likely a UX-PARITY ask, and no piece covered that reading: the Realm roster is added from a 340px-max-height scrolling list (245503) while the main deck has a card grid, search, filters and right-click detail. Build the parity — same grid, same search, same detail affordance, same ownership chrome — and implement whichever budget rule the checkpoint's decision (iv) named. If the owner chose the SHARED main+side+realm budget, the real gap is that the two systems count in separate universes (the card-detail add gate sums inDeck+inSide against ownCap at 235571-235577 and never looks at the realm roster, while the realm handler counts only its own roster at 246174-246179) and Fusion Kalons are type:'unit' (isFusionKalon 113025) so they appear in getAllDeckableCards (214072) and one owned copy legally sits in a main deck AND a Realm Deck simultaneously today. PARITY, mechanically: the Realm add surface exposes the same four affordances as the main-deck surface — a card grid (not a fixed-height list), a working text search, the ownership chrome ('🔒 Not owned', greyed row, disabled +), and the detail affordance — each asserted by a DOM query, plus an A/B screenshot pair against the main-deck surface. BUDGET, only if the owner chose shared: with exactly 1 owned Fusion Kalon, putting it in the main deck disables the Realm add button WITH A STATED REASON (assert the exact rendered reason text) and vice versa; with 2 owned copies, one in each is allowed; screenshot both directions. EDGES: admin (Infinity) must not produce NaN through the Math.min at 245475 and 246177 — assert the computed cap is a number and the buttons are enabled; and deckKeyOwnedCount SUBTRACTS camp-stationed units (59972-59974), so the driver stations a worker AFTER building a deck and asserts the stated behaviour rather than a silent invalidation. LEGACY DECKS: existing decks violating a newly-tightened rule get ONE named outcome chosen in advance — grandfathered with a flag, or refused with a specific message — and the driver constructs a violating deck and asserts THAT outcome by name. 'Reported or grandfathered' is not a bar; pick one. The old ordering said bump the knobs 'at the end of a run' but no piece had them in its files, no piece ran `npm run check:full`, and the four gauntlet drivers that pin this exact markup and are NOT in _checkall.mjs (drive-scroll-keep, drive-scale-per, drive-shufflezones, run-ai-gate) appeared only inside individual judge_methods, so nothing ran them together at the end. Run the full gate, run those four plus the effect drivers this run added, bump the five knobs ONCE, deploy, and verify at the edge.
bar: `npm run check` and `npm run check:full` both clean — no suite WORSE/SHORT/CRASH/MISSING — with the new suites from pieces 1, 11, 19 and 20 registered and passing. The four unregistered drivers plus every driver this run wrote all pass in one sequential run whose full log is the evidence. The five knobs move together and consistently: window.BUILD_VERSION (39123), sw.js CACHE_VERSION (414), node-city NC_BUILD (12), effects.js?v= (261621), handset.js?v= (261622) — and _handset_smoke.mjs:126 asserts handset's ?v= EQUALS BUILD_VERSION while _campaigns_smoke.mjs:85 pins the campaigns module ?v= as an exact literal that breaks on any bump, so both suites pass after the bump or the bump is wrong. version.txt is NOT hand-edited (deploy.mjs:86 rewrites it). After deploy, a curl of the live index.html shows the new BUILD_VERSION and the new sw.js CACHE_VERSION. Piece 18's export is taken one final time post-deploy so there is a known-good snapshot of the shipped state.

title: Acceptance gate: author a real card end-to-end and measure whether it actually got faster
goal: NEW PIECE, and the critics are right that without it the whole editor chain can be green while authoring is no faster. Nothing in the plan measured the owner's actual ask — 'neat, fits the screen, compact, easy to find' — as a task. Every other bar is a count, a ratio or a screenshot. The critic writes a card SPEC (not the builder): a named unit with two elements, a passive, an on-play effect with two knobs, a status, one learnset move and an on-kill ability. Author it from scratch at a fixed 1600x1000 through the harness, on the change and on the HEAD worktree, and measure the difference.
bar: Four numbers, both sides, same spec, same viewport, same starting state (App.editingCardId='NEW', App._fxOpen cleared): total vertical scroll distance in px to complete the card; number of <details> sections the author had to open; number of clicks; and controls VISIBLE AT REST when the editor first opens. The change must beat HEAD on scroll distance and on sections-opened, and must not be worse on clicks. The finished card must SAVE and reopen with every authored value intact — run captureEditorIntoCard and diff against the spec field by field. The spec is authored by the critic before the run and is not shown to the builder in advance; a run against a spec the builder wrote does not count. This piece has no code of its own — it is the gate the editor chain must clear before piece 22 ships it.
